texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 12.02.2018 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. On perusal of the record, it is revealed that the original single DAR, tilted Sumit Kumar Vs. Monu, was regarding two injured Sumit Kumar ans Ashish Kumar. Further, as per record, the claim petition qua such Sumit Kumar is already dismissed in default on 08.08.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor. Accordingly, the case of other injured Ashish Kumar Sharma remains. 3. As per the facts of the case, on 23.08.2017 at about 08.00 AM, injured Ashish Kumar Sharma was going to school along with other friends including such Sumit Kumar Yadav and Aman by vehicle bearing no. DL 3S-DP-4161 (motorcycle). It is further claimed by Ashish Kumar Sharma, that he was sitting behind the motorcycle as pillion rider and same was driven by Sumit Kumar. When they reached in front of BMW Show Room Badarpur to Ashram Side, Main Mathura Road, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi, back side wheel of their vehicle got punctured as such they stopped the vehicle on the side of the road, then all the sudden one vehicle bearing no. HR 55S 0350 (truck)/ offending vehicle MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 2 of 21 rpt came in high speed which was driven by R-1 in contravention of traffic rules without blowing any horn and without giving any indicator and hit the vehicle of victim side with great force from back side. That due to such forceful impact, petitioner Ashish Kumar Sharma fell down on road along with his friends and received multiple grievous injuries. The petitioner Ashish Kumar Sharma was taken to Apollo Hospital, new Delhi where his MLC no. 602/17 was prepared and thereafter, they were taken to Trauma Center AIIMS, New Delhi. 4. Accordingly the FIR in question u/s 279/338 IPC was registered in this case and even chargesheet is filed. 5. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 20.01.2020 noticing 82% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb. 6. Further, as per record, driver /R-1 Monu and owner Pradeep/ R-2 appeared. But no reply filed on their behalf. 7. But reply/ report filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, in such reply, it is stated that insurance company is not liable to pay the entire compensation, as petitioner along with two other were riding on a motorcycle which led to the accident in question. It is further submitted that due to such triple riding, tyre of the motorcycle got punctured. Further a legal offer was made which was not accepted to the petitioner and as such matter was proceeded further on merit. 8. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal as far as present petitioner is concerned: Ashish Kumar Sharma vs . Monu & Ors. on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14495151/ 2 Page No. 3 of 21 rpt and insured with R3? OPP. 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 9. As per record, Petitioner Ashish Kumar Sharma examined himself only as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 10. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 11. Further, as per record, None of the respondent led any evidence. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 4 of 21 rpt of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the Ashish Kumar Sharma vs . Monu & Ors. on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14495151/ 3 witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. 17. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place. 18. During cross examination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company, PW-1 reiterated that accident took place when their motorcycle was in a stationary condition. He further denied the suggestion that accident took place when motorcycle was moving towards left side. He further denied the suggestion that accident took place as they were riding three persons on the motorcycle and as such could not balance the same after it got punctured. 19. It is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is no eye witness other than such interested witnesses but admittedly it is a case of triple riding thus, in any case, petitioner be held for contributory negligence. 20. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that even if it is a case of triple riding then also it does not have any effect on the merit of the case and there is no question of contributory negligence as per evidence on MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 5 of 21 rpt record, the accident took place when all of them were standing when their motorcycle's tyre got punctured. It is further argued that no evidence to the contrary including by summoning and examining R-1 / driver / accused is placed on record by insurance company. 21. It is held that there is force in the argument of Ld. Counsel for petitioner. As per material on record, the accident in question took place when petitioner/ injured along with his friends were standing after their motorcycle got punctured. The insurance company failed to prove on record its defence that accident in question took place while petitioner side were driving the motorcycle with triple riding. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as Ashish Kumar Sharma vs . Monu & Ors. on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14495151/ 4 money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 24.1. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 7 of 21 rpt earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 24.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 24.7. This means that the Tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence: (i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary; MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 8 of 21 rpt (ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement; (iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person. In Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as "M. R. Krishna Murthi vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. on 5 March, 2019, (2020) 15 SCC 493: (2020) 4 SCC (Crl.) 84: 2019 SCC Online SC 315 , after dealing with various case laws relating to injury matters and death cases in case of students, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: Ashish Kumar Sharma vs . Monu & Ors. on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14495151/ 6 "24. In those cases where the victim of the accident is not an earning person but a student, while assessing the compensation for loss of future earning, the focus of the examination would be the career prospect and the likely earning of such a person in future. For example, where the claimant is pursuing a particular professional course, the poser would be: what would have been his income had he joined a service commensurating with the said course. 24.2 There may be cases where the victim is not, at that stage, MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 9 of 21 rpt doing any such course to get a particular job. He or she may be studying in a school. 31. In this background, it is claimed by learned counsel for insurance company that there is no "loss of income" at present and further there is no loss of future prospect. It is further pointed out that normally in MACT claim, under other various heads, other than these two, suitable compensation can be given as per law. It is further argued that as permanent disability is only 82% relating to right lower limb, there is no functional disability also. 32. On the other hand, it is argued by learned counsel for petitioner that at MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 11 of 21 rpt least there is 82% permanent functional disability in the present case having regard to material on record and accordingly compensation be given for future prospect. It is further argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner by placing on record the photographs of petitioner that even on visual examination, the deformity in right leg can be seen which is permanent in nature. 33. In the present case, petitioner has passed tenth class at the time of accident. p.a . having regard to the Hon'ble Supreme from the date of filing of MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. 41. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. MACT No. 175/18 Ashish Kumar Vs. Monu & Ors. Page No. 16 of 21 rpt
